text:
# RadSplat
## Overview
RadSplat initializes [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) by converting a dense point cloud derived from a trained [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) into Gaussians [S1, S2, unofficial]. It solves the topological inconsistencies and sparsity of raw [Structure-from-Motion (SfM)](#16341-structure-from-motion-sfm.md) point clouds [S1, unofficial]. The method bypasses or drastically shortens the per-scene gradient descent loop required by standard 3DGS [S1, unofficial].

## How it works
**Inputs:** A trained [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md) model for the target scene [S1, S2, unofficial]. Sparse multi-view images are used to train the initial NeRF [S1, unofficial].
**Outputs:** A set of $N$ 3D Gaussians $\{G_i\}_{i=1}^N$ with optimized position, [rotation](#19376-rotation.md), scale, opacity, and appearance parameters [S1, S2, unofficial].
**Data Structures:** The output follows the standard 3DGS primitive layout [G]. Each primitive $i$ stores: Position $\mathbf{p}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$, Rotation $q_i \in \mathbb{R}^4$ (unit quaternion), Scale $\mathbf{s}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$, Opacity $\alpha_i \in [0, 1]$, and appearance parameters (e.g., spherical harmonic coefficients) [G].
**Steps:**
1. Train a NeRF on the input sparse multi-view images to learn the scene's [implicit radiance field](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) [S1, unofficial].
2. Extract a dense point cloud from the trained NeRF [S1, unofficial].
3. Convert the extracted points into 3D Gaussians [S1, unofficial].
4. Prune Gaussians using a multi-view importance score [S2, unofficial].
**Formulas:** Not given in the sources.
**Parameters:** NeRF resolution/depth: Not given in the sources. Pruning threshold: Not given in the sources.
**Edge Cases and Pitfalls:** The initialization quality depends directly on the NeRF training outcome [S1, unofficial]. The method completely bypasses or drastically shortens the per-scene gradient descent loop [S1, unofficial].

## Operating characteristics
Rendering speed reaches 900+ [FPS](#7182-farthest-point-sampling-fps.md) with high quality [S1, unofficial]. Training time drastically shortens or bypasses the per-scene gradient descent loop [S1, unofficial]. Pruning reduces memory usage compared to dense SfM-initialized Gaussians [S2, unofficial]. Strengths include high-quality initialization, robustness to topological pitfalls of SfM, and high rendering speed [S1, S2, unofficial]. Limitations include the upfront computational cost of NeRF training [S1, unofficial]. Not given in the sources for specific memory complexity formulas.

## Background
RadSplat was introduced to improve 3DGS initialization by replacing raw SfM point clouds with NeRF-derived dense point clouds [S1, S2, unofficial]. It addresses the noise and topological errors inherent in SfM data [S1, unofficial]. The method is cited in surveys on 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md) and recent advances in the field [S1, S2, unofficial].
